task:
BUILD SLICE S3a OF THE V3 COLONY PLANNER: A READ-ONLY BODIES LIST FOR ONE SYSTEM FROM THE PUBLISHED CANONICAL GENERATION. NO SLOT PREDICTIONS. BACKEND ONLY. DO NOT TOUCH GENERATED CLIENTS.

Authority: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-30-v3-colony-planner-design.md, section 5.3 as amended in PR #932 (if not yet merged: `git fetch origin docs/planner-slot-sources && git show FETCH_HEAD:docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-30-v3-colony-planner-design.md`) and docs/development/evidence/2026-10-31-slot-formula-vs-recorded-counts.md. This text wins if they differ. Key rules: orbital slots are NEVER predicted; surface predictions come later in S3b; this slice reads ONLY canonical relations (the `v3_gen_*` schema named by the published canonical generation, plus v3_vocab and v3_meta) and NOTHING in v3_derived, v3_app or v3_spatial (step P, the governed purge, is copying v3_derived relations right now).

Do NOT touch: apps/api/src/cpe/, apps/api/src/ingest/slot_prediction.py (do not import it), routers/v3.py behaviour (importing its helpers is fine), review_main.py, sql/, apps/web/, packages/, apps/web/src/lib/api/generated, packages/api-client/src/generated (Claude regenerates the clients afterwards). No dependencies.

1. apps/api/src/routers/plan.py — add `GET /api/v1/plan/systems/{system_id}/bodies`, operation_id "listV3PlanBodies", response_model PlanBodiesV1. Path parameter exactly like routers/v3.py (`SystemId` pattern ^[0-9]{1,19}$, `_numeric_system_id` for the 422 range check). Use `pool: asyncpg.Pool = Depends(get_readonly_pool)` and resolve the schema ONCE with `current_canonical_generation(pool)` from routers/v3.py (503 when nothing is published, exactly as it does); wrap every query in routers/v3.py's `_bounded` timeout. Parameterised SQL only; the schema name comes only from current_canonical_generation (already validated by its regex). Keep the two existing plan routes database-free.
   Models (PlanModel strict base already in plan.py):
   - PlanBodiesV1 { generation_id: str; publication_sequence: str; system_id64: str; bodies: list[PlanSystemBodyV1] } — generation identity from current_canonical_generation's GenerationV1, so the page can tell a republished catalogue.
   - PlanSystemBodyV1 { body_id: str (body_pk as decimal string, same as BodyV1.body_id); name: str; direct_parent_body_id: str | None; body_type: str | None (v3_vocab.body_type.public_code); is_main_star: bool | None; is_landable: bool | None; radius_km: float | None; surface_gravity_g: float | None; surface_temperature_k: float | None; atmosphere: str | None (v3_vocab.atmosphere_classification.display_name, e.g. "Thin Ammonia", "No atmosphere"; NULL id stays null = unknown, never coerced to "No atmosphere"); terraforming_state: str | None (v3_vocab.terraforming_state.display_name); volcanism: str | None (v3_vocab.volcanism_type.display_name); distance_from_arrival_ls: float | None; has_rings: bool (true when the body has at least one row in {schema}.rings with kind = 'RING'; BELT rows do not count); geological_signals: int; biological_signals: int (sums of {schema}.body_signal_current.signal_count for that body's signal types whose v3_vocab.signal_type.display_name is 'Geological' / 'Biological' — check the vocabulary in apps/importer/src/v3_spansh/adapter.py VOCABULARY and match by display_name, not a hard-coded id; 0 when there are no such rows); signals_complete: bool | None (bodies.signals_complete, so the page can tell "0 found" from "not surveyed"); lifecycle_state: str }.
   Ordering: bodies ordered by body_pk, like listV3SystemBodies. Return every body row for the system exactly as listV3SystemBodies does (same WHERE, no extra lifecycle filter) so the two routes agree on membership.
   Use three queries at most (bodies with LEFT JOINs to the four vocab tables; ring presence grouped by body_pk; geological/biological signal sums grouped by body_pk), each filtered by system_id64 = $1, combined in Python. An unknown system returns 200 with an empty bodies list (same membership behaviour as listV3SystemBodies, which returns []).

2. Tests:
   A. tests/test_plan_bodies_postgres.py — PostgreSQL test following tests/test_v3_inspect_share_travel_postgres.py exactly (`from tests.ratings_v4_pg_fixture import canonical_database`, RATINGS_V4_VALIDATION_DATABASE_URL, module-scoped database fixture, asyncpg pool, httpx ASGITransport app with app.state.limiter = limiter and the plan router). CI's PostgreSQL 18 lanes pick it up automatically because it names canonical_database. Assert, for a fixture system that has bodies, rings and body signals (choose one from the fixture, e.g. the SOL constant the other test uses, and add a second system if needed to cover rings with kind RING and BELT):
      - 200, generation_id/publication_sequence equal the published generation, system_id64 echoed;
      - body membership and order equal GET /api/v1/systems/{id}/bodies (call both routes in the same test) and every shared field (body_id, name, direct_parent_body_id, body_type, is_main_star, is_landable, radius_km, distance_from_arrival_ls, lifecycle_state) is identical;
      - atmosphere/terraforming_state/volcanism equal the vocab display_name for the body's ids (query the fixture DB directly to build the expectation), and stay null where the id is null;
      - has_rings true exactly for bodies with a RING row; a body with only a BELT row (if the fixture has one; otherwise insert one inside the test transaction-safe way the other tests use, or skip that assertion with a clear message) is false;
      - geological_signals/biological_signals equal the sums computed directly from body_signal_current joined to signal_type display_name;
      - unknown system id -> 200 with bodies == []; '18446744073709551615' -> 422; no published generation -> 503 (reuse the pattern from test_v3_system_routes_fail_closed_without_a_published_generation).
      You cannot run PostgreSQL on the runner: write the test carefully against the fixture loader (tests/fixtures/ratings_v4_sources, domain.ratings_v4_canonical.load_source_fixture, scripts/dev/v3_canonical_bootstrap.py) so the expectations are computed from the database, not guessed; Claude runs it against PostgreSQL afterwards.
   B. tests/test_plan_router.py — extend the existing no-database tests: the bodies route is in the OpenAPI document with operation id listV3PlanBodies; it is the ONLY plan route with a database dependency (get_readonly_pool), and catalogue/evaluate still have none (update the existing no-database assertion accordingly, keep it strict for those two); a static check that plan.py's SQL text never mentions v3_derived, v3_app or v3_spatial.
